message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"de33a7dea29d39385ccf211c1be6994847acb64a31e9f7f0730775680d06222f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-in-class-std:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"2800087d52ca58455ac6dac735a6e1bd60a4442f9e09c2356d96bd9ed8102504","units":[{"unit_id":"sec03-u01","module_id":"sec03-m01","objective_ids":["sec03-u01"],"title":{"text":"Restrictions on your credential","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A restriction is a legal condition on your driving, so breaking it is driving outside your license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F03","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Vision results cause most restrictions, which makes the vision screening one of the most important steps in getting licensed.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ella passes her vision screening only with her glasses, and her new license shows restriction B.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Restriction B means she must wear glasses or contact lenses whenever she drives.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"result":{"text":"Ella keeps her glasses in the car and wears them on every drive, because driving without them breaks her restriction.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking restriction F is about the driver's eyesight.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04"]},"correction":{"text":"Restriction F is about the vehicle: it must have outside mirrors or a rearview camera whenever the holder drives.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"B for both lenses, F for fitted mirrors, G for daylight.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver's license carries restriction G. May the driver make a trip home at nine at night?","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},"answer":{"text":"No. Restriction G limits the holder to driving in daylight only.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},"rationale":{"text":"G is the daylight-only restriction, so night driving breaks it.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Reading your restrictions","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Where restrictions appear.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F06"]},{"text":"What B, F and G mean.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F06"]},{"text":"Disability restrictions.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on restrictions. A restriction is a condition printed on your credential that you must follow every time you drive. In this lesson you will learn where restrictions appear on an Indiana card, why the vision screening is the most common reason a driver ends up with one, and what three of the most common vision-related restrictions require. You will also see how BMV examiners handle restrictions for drivers whose disability affects how they operate a standard vehicle, including licenses that name the equipment a driver must use.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Where restrictions appear","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lower left corner of the card.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Meanings printed on the back.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Vision is the most common source.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Restrictions and endorsements appear in the lower left corner of an Indiana credential, and their meanings are printed on the back of the card, so you can always check what a code means without looking it up. Vision screening results are the most common source of restrictions on learner's permits and driver's licenses. That makes sense: if you need corrective lenses to see well enough to drive, the license says so. If you are ever unsure what your own restriction requires, turn the card over and read the explanation printed there before you drive.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Restrictions B, F and G","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"B: glasses or contact lenses.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"F: outside mirrors or a rearview camera.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"G: daylight driving only.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Three restrictions come up often. Restriction B means the driver must wear glasses or contact lenses when driving. Restriction F means the vehicle must have outside mirrors or a rearview camera whenever the holder drives, so it is a rule about the car rather than about the driver's eyes. Restriction G limits the holder to driving in daylight only. Notice how different they are. B is about what you wear, F is about what the vehicle has, and G is about when you may drive. Each one applies on every trip, not just on long drives or at the exam.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Disability restrictions","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Examiners decide.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},{"text":"Specific equipment may be required.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},{"text":"Accommodations can be named.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some drivers have a disability that affects normal operation of a standard vehicle. For them, BMV examiners decide whether to issue a restricted license, and that license may require specific equipment or other accommodations. A restricted license for a driver with disabilities can name the particular equipment the driver must use in the vehicle. The point of these restrictions is not to keep people off the road but to make sure the vehicle and the driver are set up to drive safely. As with any restriction, the conditions printed on the card apply every time the person drives.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Driver rule or vehicle rule","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03","sec03-F05","sec03-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: F means vision.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03","sec03-F05","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"F is about mirrors or a camera.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03","sec03-F05","sec03-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Because restrictions so often come from the vision screening, learners assume every restriction is about the driver's eyes. Restriction B is, since it requires glasses or contact lenses. Restriction F is not. It requires the vehicle to have outside mirrors or a rearview camera whenever the holder drives. Restriction G is about time, limiting the driver to daylight. When a question names a restriction letter, ask whether it describes what the driver wears, what the car must have, or when driving is allowed, and the right answer usually follows.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03","sec03-F05","sec03-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a night trip","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"License shows restriction G.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},{"text":"Drive home at nine at night?","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a driver's license carries restriction G, and the driver wants to drive home from a friend's house at nine at night. Is that allowed? Recall what G means. Restriction G limits the holder to driving in daylight only, so a nine o'clock night drive breaks the restriction. The answer is no. Compare that with restriction B, which would only require glasses or contacts, and restriction F, which would only require mirrors or a camera on the vehicle. If you allowed the trip, review the daylight-only meaning of G.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Restrictions recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lower left, explained on back.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},{"text":"B lenses, F mirrors, G daylight.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},{"text":"Examiners set disability terms.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. Restrictions and endorsements sit in the lower left corner of your credential, with their meanings on the back, and vision results are the most common reason for a restriction. Restriction B means wear glasses or contacts, F means the vehicle needs outside mirrors or a rearview camera, and G means daylight driving only. For drivers whose disability affects normal vehicle operation, BMV examiners decide whether to issue a restricted license, which may require and name specific equipment or accommodations. Every restriction applies every time you drive.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-R14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u02","module_id":"sec03-m02","objective_ids":["sec03-u02"],"title":{"text":"Reading the code chart","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Codes are how your credential tells police and examiners what you may and may not drive.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},{"text":"Some letters and numbers mean different things as restrictions and as endorsements, so reading the chart carefully avoids mistakes.","fact_ids":["sec03-R01","sec03-R03"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Maya's ID card shows endorsement B, and her friend says that means she must wear glasses.","fact_ids":["sec03-R01"]},"reasoning":{"text":"As a license restriction B means glasses or contacts, but as an ID card endorsement B means motor driven cycle.","fact_ids":["sec03-R01","sec03-F07"]},"result":{"text":"Maya's endorsement B lets her ride a motor driven cycle; it says nothing about glasses.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R01"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the number two always means the same thing on a license.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03"]},"correction":{"text":"Endorsement two means for-hire, while restriction two marks an HTV conditional license.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F07","sec03-F10"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Same symbol, check the column: restriction or endorsement.","fact_ids":["sec03-R01","sec03-R03"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A base license shows restriction code six. What does it mean?","fact_ids":["sec03-F08"]},"answer":{"text":"The holder must use an interlock device.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08"]},"rationale":{"text":"On the base license chart, six stands for an interlock device and eight for a medical condition.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"A chart full of codes","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Endorsements add privileges.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Restrictions add conditions.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Some symbols repeat.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on the Indiana code chart. Your credential uses short letters and numbers to say what extra vehicles you may drive and what conditions you must follow. Endorsements add privileges, such as riding a motorcycle or driving for hire. Restrictions add conditions, such as needing an adaptive device. The tricky part is that a few symbols show up in more than one place with different meanings. By the end of this lesson you will be able to read the main codes and avoid the classic mix-ups between restriction letters and endorsement letters.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Endorsement codes","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"License: L motorcycle, two for-hire.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"ID card: B motor driven cycle.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"On a base driver's license, endorsement L stands for motorcycle and endorsement two stands for for-hire. On an ID card, endorsement B stands for motor driven cycle. Those three cover the endorsements you are most likely to meet as a new driver. Notice that the letter B also appears on the license chart as a restriction, where it means glasses or contact lenses. As an ID card endorsement, B means motor driven cycle instead. So whenever you see B, check whether it sits among the restrictions on a license or among the endorsements on an ID card.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Restriction codes","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"C aid, D prosthetic, J limits.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Six interlock, eight medical.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Three, seven, nine on both card types.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Base license restriction codes include C for a mechanical aid or adaptive device, D for a prosthetic aid, J for specific limitations, six for an interlock device and eight for a medical condition. Some codes appear on both base licenses and ID cards: three means photo exempt, seven means seat belt exempt and nine means lawful temporary resident. There are motorcycle and condition codes too. Restriction H limits motorcycle riding to a three-wheel bike, S limits it to a motorcycle with a sidecar, two marks an HTV conditional license, and five means the holder may drive only under specific conditions.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Symbols that repeat","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-R03","sec03-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"G daylight versus J limitations.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-R03","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Two: for-hire or HTV conditional.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-R03","sec03-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. A few symbols on the chart look alike or repeat. Restriction G means daylight driving only, while restriction J means specific limitations, and the two letters are easy to swap. The number two is the bigger trap. As an endorsement on a base license, two means for-hire. As a restriction, two marks an HTV conditional license, which is a very different situation. And B, as we saw, means glasses or contacts as a restriction but motor driven cycle as an ID card endorsement. Always ask which column a code sits in before deciding what it means.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-R03","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a restriction code","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Base license shows code six.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},{"text":"What does it require?","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a base Indiana license shows restriction code six. What does that code mean? Run through the restriction codes on the base license chart. C is a mechanical aid or adaptive device, D is a prosthetic aid, J is specific limitations, six is an interlock device and eight is a medical condition. So code six means the holder must use an interlock device. If you guessed a medical condition, that is code eight, and if you guessed seat belt exempt, that is code seven, which appears on both licenses and ID cards.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Codes at a glance","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R02","sec03-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Endorsements: L, two, B on ID.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R02","sec03-R03"]},{"text":"Restrictions: letters and numbers.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R02","sec03-R03"]},{"text":"Check the column.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R02","sec03-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. On a base license, endorsement L is motorcycle and endorsement two is for-hire; on an ID card, endorsement B is motor driven cycle. Base license restrictions include C for a mechanical aid, D for a prosthetic aid, J for specific limitations, six for an interlock and eight for a medical condition, while three, seven and nine, photo exempt, seat belt exempt and lawful temporary resident, appear on both licenses and ID cards. H, S, two and five cover three-wheel bikes, sidecars, HTV conditional licenses and specific conditions. Same symbol, check the column.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R02","sec03-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u03","module_id":"sec03-m03","objective_ids":["sec03-u03"],"title":{"text":"Motorcycle permit and endorsement","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Riding a motorcycle legally takes either a permit with strict limits or a full endorsement on your license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F16"]},{"text":"The permit has a short life and a renewal cap, so planning to earn the endorsement in time matters.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-F14"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Jake gets a motorcycle learner's permit and wants to give his sister a ride to school at seven in the morning.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A permit holder must wear a helmet, may not carry passengers, and may ride only within the daylight window around sunrise and sunset.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12"]},"result":{"text":"Jake may ride alone with a helmet in the daylight window, but he may not carry his sister on a permit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a new resident with an out-of-state motorcycle endorsement must retake the riding skills exam.","fact_ids":["sec03-R09"]},"correction":{"text":"A new resident with an out-of-state motorcycle credential takes only the motorcycle knowledge exam.","fact_ids":["sec03-R09","sec03-F17"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Permit: helmet, solo, daylight; endorsement: course or both exams.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Jake wants to carry a passenger while riding on his motorcycle learner's permit. Is that allowed?","fact_ids":["sec03-F12"]},"answer":{"text":"No. A motorcycle permit holder may not carry passengers.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12"]},"rationale":{"text":"Permit limits are a helmet, no passengers and riding only in the daylight window.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Two steps to riding","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"The motorcycle permit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]},{"text":"The motorcycle endorsement.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on motorcycle permits and endorsements. If you want to ride a motorcycle in Indiana, there are two credentials to know. The motorcycle learner's permit lets you practice with strict limits, and the motorcycle endorsement on your driver's license lets you ride without those limits. In this lesson you will learn how to get the permit and what it allows, how long it lasts, the routes to the endorsement for first-time riders and new residents, and how the endorsement is renewed along with your license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Getting and using the permit","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Need a valid license and the motorcycle exam.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12"]},{"text":"Helmet always.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12"]},{"text":"No passengers; daylight window only.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"A motorcycle learner's permit requires a valid Indiana driver's license and a passed knowledge exam based on the Motorcycle Operator's Manual. So the motorcycle permit is built on top of a regular license, not instead of one. Once you hold it, three limits apply. You must wear a helmet, you may not carry passengers, and you may ride only in the daylight window that runs from one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset. These limits protect new riders while they build skill, and they apply on every ride while you hold only the permit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Permit validity and limits","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid one year.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-F14"]},{"text":"At most three issues in five years.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-F14"]},{"text":"Run out: wait a year or take a course.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"A motorcycle learner's permit is valid for one year, and it can be issued or renewed no more than three times in a five-year period. That cap is there to push riders toward the endorsement rather than riding on permits indefinitely. If you do not earn the endorsement before the renewed motorcycle permit expires, you must wait one year for a new permit, or complete a Ride Safe Indiana safety course. Plan your practice and testing so you earn the endorsement while your permit is still valid, and you will avoid the one-year wait altogether.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Earning the endorsement","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F15","sec03-R13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Ride Safe Indiana course, or both exams.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F15","sec03-R13"]},{"text":"Course before a first license: endorse at once.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F15","sec03-R13"]},{"text":"Courses strongly encouraged.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F15","sec03-R13"]}],"narration":{"text":"A motorcycle endorsement requires, at any age, either a completed Ride Safe Indiana safety course or passing both the motorcycle knowledge exam and the riding skills exam. A first-time license applicant aged sixteen or older who has completed a motorcycle safety course can receive the motorcycle endorsement together with the new license. The BMV strongly encourages motorcycle safety courses from Ride Safe Indiana providers, which are listed at RideSafeIndiana.com. For a beginner the course route is often simpler, since it replaces the two motorcycle exams and teaches riding skills at the same time.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16","sec03-F15","sec03-R13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Transfers and renewal","fact_ids":["sec03-F17","sec03-R09","sec03-F18","sec03-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"New residents: knowledge exam only.","fact_ids":["sec03-F17","sec03-R09","sec03-F18","sec03-R07"]},{"text":"Endorsement lasts as long as the license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F17","sec03-R09","sec03-F18","sec03-R07"]},{"text":"Renew up to two years early.","fact_ids":["sec03-F17","sec03-R09","sec03-F18","sec03-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"A new resident holding a valid motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle license from another state adds the Indiana endorsement after passing only the motorcycle knowledge exam, with no riding skills exam. Once you have it, the motorcycle endorsement lasts as long as your driver's license. The license can be renewed with the endorsement up to two years early, at a branch or online, and an unexpired endorsement carries no extra fee at renewal. That makes the endorsement easy to keep once earned, as long as you renew your license before it expires.","fact_ids":["sec03-F17","sec03-R09","sec03-F18","sec03-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two transfer traps","fact_ids":["sec03-R09","sec03-F17","sec03-F16","sec03-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: transfers retake the riding test.","fact_ids":["sec03-R09","sec03-F17","sec03-F16","sec03-F12"]},{"text":"Trap: permits can carry passengers.","fact_ids":["sec03-R09","sec03-F17","sec03-F16","sec03-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here are two traps. First, new residents. People assume that moving to Indiana means starting from scratch on a motorcycle. A new resident with a valid out-of-state motorcycle endorsement or license takes only the motorcycle knowledge exam, not the riding skills exam. First-time riders are different, since they need a Ride Safe Indiana course or both exams. Second, permit passengers. A motorcycle permit holder may not carry passengers at all, even a family member, and must wear a helmet and stay within the daylight window. Keep the transfer rule and the permit limits separate.","fact_ids":["sec03-R09","sec03-F17","sec03-F16","sec03-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a passenger ride","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Motorcycle permit only.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]},{"text":"Passenger on the back?","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Jake holds a motorcycle learner's permit and wants to carry his sister on the back to school. Is that allowed? Recall the three permit limits.
